chunks: Hammad ibn Isa narrated from Rabiʿ ibn Abdullah from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
When a man dies, his sword, his Qur'an, his ring, his books, his saddle, and his clothing belong to his eldest child. If the eldest is a daughter, then they belong to the eldest of the sons.

key_terms.أَكْبَرِ وُلْدِهِ: his eldest child, the primary recipient named in the ruling
key_terms.الذُّكُورِ: the male children, relevant when the eldest child is a daughter
key_terms.خَاتَمُهُ: his ring as part of the specifically assigned belongings
key_terms.رَحْلُهُ: his saddle or riding gear counted among his personal effects
key_terms.كُتُبُهُ: his books included among the inherited items
key_terms.كِسْوَتُهُ: his clothing assigned under this inheritance ruling
key_terms.مُصْحَفُهُ: his Qur'an codex among the designated inherited personal effects

ai.seo_question: Who inherits a deceased man’s personal items such as his sword, Qur'an, ring, books, saddle, and clothing?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about specific personal effects of a deceased man, assigning them to the eldest child. If the eldest child is a daughter, these items are instead assigned to the eldest male child.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5746 - Hammad ibn Isa narrated from Rabiʿ ibn Abdullah from Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) who said:
"When a man dies, his sword, his Qur'an, his ring, his books, his saddle, and his clothing belong to his eldest child. If the eldest is a daughter, then they belong to the eldest of the sons."
